willcox_benchmarks.note: Benchmark rate = total survey change / years between first and last survey (some since 1943-1991). Radar = 2016-2026 vertical-equivalent rate at the benchmark.

willcox_forward.note: Rate map from 13 dates before 2023 only. Positives: field-surveyed fissures added to the state map between Jan 2023 and May 2026 (65 features, 32 cells of 270 m).

mexico_nisar.note: Each cell counts 80 m pixels. Sentinel-1 covers 2016-2026, NISAR 2025-2026, so the spread mixes noise with real change.

mexico_gps.note: Radar and GPS both along the radar line of sight, both relative to station TNGF, Dec 2017 to Mar 2019 (71 radar dates).

phoenix_benchmarks.note: Survey rates are multi-decade vertical averages (mostly 1997 onward); radar is 2016-2026 along the line of sight. Rank agrees; sizes are not comparable.

chennai.note: Smallest detectable rate = 2 sigma / record length. Fixed floor: noise stays at today's level. Random walk: independent pair noise adds up.

truth.note: GPS vertical rates (Nevada Geodetic Laboratory, robust slope over the radar period) against the radar rate at each station. Radar is converted from line of sight with one angle (39 deg), good to about 12 %. At places with three or more stations the median difference is removed first, because the radar is relative and GPS is absolute.
